metadata.title: [BUG]: Authorization-code token exchange ignores `token_endpoint_auth_method`,   breaking DCR with strict OAuth 2.1 providers (e.g. Datadog)
metadata.author: mvgijssel

description:
### Summary

  When ContextForge registers a confidential OAuth client via DCR and the authorization server
  defaults the client to `token_endpoint_auth_method: "client_secret_basic"` (the RFC 7591 §2
  default), the subsequent authorization-code token exchange fails with `400 invalid_client`. The
  stored `token_endpoint_auth_method` is silently ignored — credentials are always sent in the form
  body (`client_secret_post`).

  This breaks any OAuth 2.1 provider that strictly enforces the registered auth method. Confirmed
  against Datadog's MCP server (`https://mcp.datadoghq.com`).

  Related but distinct from #3991, which proposes UI exposure of `token_endpoint_auth_method` and
  incorrectly states the backend already honors it.

  ### Reproduction

  1. Add a gateway pointing at an OAuth 2.1 provider that defaults DCR clients to
  `client_secret_basic`, with only the **Issuer** set (no client_id/client_secret). DCR
  auto-registration runs.

     Example provider: Datadog MCP, `https://mcp.datadoghq.com/api/unstable/mcp-server/mcp`.

  2. Trigger the OAuth flow. DCR succeeds, `/authorize` returns a code, but `/oauth/callback` fails:

     ```
     ❌ OAuth Authorization Failed
     Failed to exchange code for token after 3 attempts:
     Client error '400 Bad Request' for url '.../token'
     ```

  3. With debug logging added to surface the response body, the provider replies:

     ```json
     {"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Invalid client_secret"}
     ```

  4. Manual probe against the same endpoint with the same `client_id` + `client_secret` from
  `registered_oauth_clients`:

     | Auth style | Result |
     |---|---|
     | Credentials in form body (`client_secret_post`) | `400 invalid_client / Invalid client_secret`
  |
     | `Authorization: Basic` header (`client_secret_basic`) | `400 invalid_grant / Invalid
  authorization code` (gets past auth) |

     The secret is correct; only the *delivery method* is wrong.

  ### Root cause

  `mcpgateway/services/oauth_manager.py::_exchange_code_for_tokens` (around line 1416 in v1.0.0)
  builds the token request as:

  ```python
  token_data = {
      "grant_type": "authorization_code",
      "code": code,
      "redirect_uri": redirect_uri,
      "client_id": client_id,
  }
  if client_secret:
      token_data["client_secret"] = client_secret
  ```

  …and posts via `_post_token_request(url, data=token_data)` — so credentials always go in the form
  body. The function never reads `token_endpoint_auth_method` from `registered_oauth_clients` or from
  `credentials`. The same issue exists in `exchange_code_for_token` (~line 580). The DCR call in
  `dcr_service` also does not explicitly request `token_endpoint_auth_method: "client_secret_post"`,
  so it inherits whatever default the AS picks — `client_secret_basic` per RFC 7591 §2.

  `refresh_token` (~line 1538) has the same shape and is likely affected too.

  ### Why other providers don't trip this

  Auth0, Okta, Google, Microsoft, etc. accept either form for clients registered as
  `client_secret_basic` — they're lenient per RFC 6749 §2.3.1. Datadog (and presumably other strict
  OAuth 2.1 servers) enforce the registered method. The mismatch is invisible until ContextForge meets
   a strict server.

  ### Proposed fix

  Honor `token_endpoint_auth_method` in `_exchange_code_for_tokens` (and `refresh_token`, and the
  non-PKCE path):

  ```python
  method = runtime_credentials.get("token_endpoint_auth_method", "client_secret_post")
  auth = None
  if client_secret and method == "client_secret_basic":
      auth = (client_id, client_secret)
      token_data.pop("client_secret", None)
      # client_id may also be omitted from the body when sent via Basic — RFC 6749 §2.3.1
  elif method == "none":
      token_data.pop("client_secret", None)
  # else client_secret_post — current behavior

  response = await self._post_token_request(token_url, token_data, auth=auth, ...)
  ```

  Additionally, in `dcr_service`, explicitly send `"token_endpoint_auth_method": "client_secret_post"`
   in the registration request so new DCR clients match ContextForge's current emit behavior — until
  the broader fix above lands.

  ### Workaround

  Pre-register the client out-of-band with `"token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"` (public client +
  PKCE) or `"client_secret_post"`, then paste the returned `client_id` into ContextForge and leave
  Client Secret empty (for `none`).

  ### Environment

  - ContextForge: `ghcr.io/ibm/mcp-context-forge:v1.0.0`
  - Provider: Datadog MCP server, US1 (`https://mcp.datadoghq.com`)
  - Transport: streamable HTTP
  - Grant: authorization_code with PKCE (S256)

comments.author: bogdanmariusc10
comments.body:
Thanks for the detailed bug report, @mvgijssel ! Bug confirmed: `token_endpoint_auth_method` is not being honored in one of the authorization code exchange paths.

### Confirmed Issue

The [`exchange_code_for_token()`](https://github.com/ibm/mcp-context-forge/blob/main/mcpgateway/services/oauth_manager.py#L620-L673) method (non-PKCE authorization code flow) always sends client credentials in the POST body, ignoring the `token_endpoint_auth_method` setting stored in the database.

**Current behavior (lines 640-649):**
```python
token_data = {
    "grant_type": "authorization_code",
    "code": code,
    "redirect_uri": redirect_uri,
    "client_id": client_id,
}

if client_secret:
    token_data["client_secret"] = client_secret
```

This hardcodes `client_secret_post` behavior and will fail with OAuth 2.1 providers that strictly enforce `client_secret_basic` (like Datadog).

### Good News

The PKCE path ([`_exchange_code_for_tokens()`](https://github.com/ibm/mcp-context-forge/blob/main/mcpgateway/services/oauth_manager.py#L1470-L1550)) already implements this correctly:
- Line 1486 reads `token_endpoint_auth_method` from credentials
- Lines 1496-1510 properly handle both `client_secret_basic` (Authorization header) and `client_secret_post` (form body)

The [`refresh_token()`](https://github.com/ibm/mcp-context-forge/blob/main/mcpgateway/services/oauth_manager.py#L1554-L1610) method also handles this correctly (lines 1596-1610).

### Recommended Fix

Apply the same pattern from `_exchange_code_for_tokens()` to `exchange_code_for_token()`:

```python
# Check token_endpoint_auth_method from runtime credentials
use_basic_auth = runtime_credentials.get("token_endpoint_auth_method", "client_secret_post") == "client_secret_basic"

token_data = {
    "grant_type": "authorization_code",
    "code": code,
    "redirect_uri": redirect_uri,
}
headers = {}

if use_basic_auth and client_secret:
    headers["Authorization"] = self._build_basic_auth_header(client_id, client_secret)
else:
    token_data["client_id"] = client_id
    if client_secret:
        token_data["client_secret"] = client_secret
```

This ensures consistent behavior across all token exchange paths and maintains compatibility with strict OAuth 2.1 providers.

I'll open a PR for this fix.
